reviews.text: While passing through for the Sausage Walk, we took the opportunity to discover Casa del Doggo. Such a lovely place, where the term "dog-friendly" truly applies. The human cookies were delicious, the cappuccino too, and apparently the one for dogs as well! We also bought some pastries to take home for afternoon tea. Elie felt right at home! Absolutely fantastic 😁
Birthday cake approved by Floki 🎂🥳 …

Dog-friendly, but definitely not human-friendly! Two visits, two disasters. The staff weren't smiling, the place wasn't air-conditioned, and we really felt like we were bothering them. They served us while half-asleep on their phones.

I ordered a matcha, a biscuit, and a puppuccino for my dog. Five minutes later, she told me she had to go walk her dog and asked us to leave. What a disaster!
Great welcome, very nice place, we will be back.

August 2026 Update: We visited Casa del Doggo three times: in January, February, and August. In January, we loved it and even highlighted in our review how great the concept was. Our dog had a lot of fun, and we were able to take our time. Enthralled by the experience, we tried to return in February and on August 1st. In February, we found the doors closed at 4 pm (closing time was listed as 7 pm, but this wasn't announced on social media). Thinking that emergencies can happen, we tried again yesterday. And once again, the doors were closed at 5 pm. Again, social media indicated a 7 pm closing time. There was no announcement either (which we had taken the precaution of checking given our previous experience). So, out of three visits, we weren't able to enjoy the place twice! Either we were incredibly unlucky, or this is a far too common practice. It's a real shame because the location is fantastic, but unfortunately, it's too unpredictable, especially when you're coming from far away. We hope to find similar but more reliable places in Paris in the future.
A unique, welcoming, and friendly place. We celebrated our little prince's first birthday there. An experience worth trying.

A wonderful experience this Friday afternoon at Casa del Diogo! The saleswoman was pleasant, smiling, and truly very kind. My dog ​​was warmly welcomed and loved the little pastries made just for him. The shop is air-conditioned, which is very welcome, especially in hot weather, and being able to bring your dog is a real bonus. I highly recommend it!

We traveled to an event that was canceled at the last minute without any prior notice. Upon arrival, there was no one to greet us or explain the reason for the cancellation.

We drove 45 minutes and played along, buying a drink and some dog treats. I ordered a strawberry matcha—€7 for a matcha with water (no strawberry), and canned iced tea for €7.
It looked nicer on Instagram than in real life.
A pleasant and welcoming space; a moment of well-being for the dog and comfortable relaxation for us.

Nice place to have a coffee while the dogs play together. Delicious pastries are available for both dogs and humans 😋
My only complaint: the milk for hot drinks seems to be stored at room temperature with the milk container constantly plugged into the machine. Hygiene issues! …
Excellent experience, our little Mango loved it, and so did we! Thanks again to the kind staff.

So what can we say about this amazing place reserved for our beloved pets!

We adore the kindness of the person who greets us with a wonderful smile, the concept, the cozy atmosphere, the packages offered... Our dogs love it, and so do the dog moms! 😊🥰🥰
Go for it!

A superb meeting place for dog lovers. Our dachshund was able to meet other dachshunds before the Paris Sausage Walk 2025. The pastry for our dog looked delicious because he devoured it ☺️ I recommend it; these dog-friendly places are lacking in many cities.
A friendly space for socializing with little treats for our best friends! Affordable and a pleasant time
Very nice and very friendly place!
A fantastic restaurant for dogs! Audrey and I are so happy about this discovery 😊 …
Great place!

I came to try out this concept with my dog, and while the place is admittedly small, it's quite pleasant at first glance. However, my experience was mixed.

My dog ​​had a small accident inside, for which I immediately apologized. The saleswoman then asked me to put him on a leash to prevent it from happening again. I found this reaction a bit inappropriate, especially for a place that presents itself as being dedicated to dogs.

I understand the need to maintain certain boundaries, but I think a little more tolerance and flexibility would be appreciated in this type of establishment. When you create a space for dogs, you expect them to have a certain amount of freedom.

I stumbled upon Casa del Doggo quite by chance. Being in Paris with my dog, I was looking for a nice place and found this spot just 5 minutes from where I was, so I went straight in! 😄 And what a pleasure it was! A warm and welcoming place for us and our dogs. My cappuccino was also delicious. Thanks again, we'll be back! 🥰 …

Fun and friendly atmosphere with our canine friends ❤️.....and a very warm welcome from the staff 🌺
For animal lovers, I highly recommend this place 🥰 …

My chihuahua and I love this place 💖 We come every week. Great place for dogs to meet. The girls are very, very nice. …

The idea is nice, but the atmosphere depends a lot on the owners' training, as some comments have mentioned. You don't bring a fearful or otherwise anxious dog to an enclosed space to socialize it. The dog needs to be able to leave the situation and go away if necessary. I even had a dog owner tell me his female dog was in heat?! (The poor thing was trying to scare the males away by barking.) Why bring a female dog in heat to a dog café? Other owners say their dog is friendly (and I believe them; they can handle encounters outside very well), but the dog starts fighting as soon as they're greeted. The café idea is nice, but it's more appealing to humans than it is for the dogs in reality, because an enclosed space encourages bad behavior. Every time I've been, I've seen at least one dog that needed a trainer more than a pastry.

I would also recommend not serving chocolate cakes, even if they are intended for humans, as falling crumbs can be toxic to dogs.

The staff is friendly.
